physical_harm: Death due to aluminium phosphide poisoning
key_evidence_accepted: The deceased was subjected to harassment for dowry not only by the husband (appellant no.1) but also by the parents-in-law (appellant nos.2 & 3) till almost immediately before her death. The death occurred due to aluminium phosphide poisoning, and the evidence indicates that the harassment was for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
witness_credibility: The court believed the witnesses who had consistently supported the prosecution version of harassment, maltreatment and misbehavior by the appellants with Rachhpal Kaur on account of her allegedly bringing insufficient dowry.

legal_representation.accused: Nagendra Rai, Rishi Malhotra, Gopi Raman
legal_representation.state: V. Madhukar, AAG, Paritosh Anil, Anvita Cowshish, Srajita Mathur, Kuldip Sing

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was subjected to harassment for dowry by the husband and parents-in-law, leading to her death due to aluminium phosphide poisoning. They contended that the FIR was not delayed, the demand for dowry was made and satisfied, and the ingredients of Section 304-B IPC were made out.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was a delay in lodging the FIR, the demand for dowry was an afterthought not mentioned in the FIR, and the ingredients of Section 304-B IPC were not proximate to the death.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act, 1872, and the provisions of Section 304-B of the Penal Code, 1860, to establish the case of dowry death.
precedent_relied_upon: Gurrnail Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 11 SCALE 224, Jitender Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) 6 SCC 204, Tarsem Singh v. State of Punjab (2008) 16 SCC 155, and Bachni Devi v. State of Haryana (2011) 4 SCC 427
sentencing_rationale: The court imposed a minimum of seven years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 304-B IPC, as the law prescribes no reduction in sentence for any reason, and the appellants were responsible for the death of the deceased.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court considered the aggravating factors of the appellants' responsibility for the death of the deceased through aluminium phosphide poisoning and the trauma caused to the victim's family.
